problem.title: One continuation family and its planar Floquet critical graph
problem.question: Decide whether the Li--Li--Liao unequal-mass non-hierarchical catalog is one continuation-connected family or several, and on each component compute the planar linear-Floquet critical graph in mass space: mechanism-labeled edges, mixed organizers, folds, and independently verified qualitative events.
problem.scope: Planar linear Floquet stability for the frozen Li--Li--Liao unequal-mass non-hierarchical catalog and its branch-preserving continuations; not the general three-body problem, spatial stability, KAM stability, or a theorem of nonlinear stability.
problem.success_criterion: SOLVED only when Gate C is passed, every mechanism word used in the paper has an independent BigFloat/physical bind, the critical graph is release_ready, completeness screens are frozen, novelty is same-day, and --require-solved passes.
problem.baseline: Li, Li & Liao (2021), arXiv:2007.10184 / Science China Physics, Mechanics & Astronomy 64, 219511. The published 135,445-orbit catalog and its 13,315 stable labels are baseline facts, not ATLAS discoveries.

decision.summary: OPEN. Gate C passed: the frozen catalog is supported as one continuation-connected component and the 2023 two-set reading rests on a projection we show to be folded and non-injective. Gate A passed for the three mechanism words the paper is allowed to use: a bracketed physical +1 crossing, a bracketed opposite-Krein Hamiltonian-Hopf collision, and three (4,4) mixed roots. Every one of the 620 published adjacent S/U cells has been localized once and assigned to one of seven catalog polylines; six further event-sign polylines carry the label-invisible 2→1 / 1→2 curves the S/U census cannot see; and sixteen mixed continuation germs are frozen (four for each of the three headline organizers plus four the retained secondary-right node owes in its own right). That is a covering of the published cell list plus the certified event-sign lattice, not a finished critical graph. As assembled, the polyline incidence still leaves three connected components, but there are no unclassified edge ends and secondary_left_birth is a projection_fold. Completeness IS now frozen, but only in the bounded sense the known_limitations spell out: a 0.0253% neck rectangle plus one 0.002539% off-grid pocket. Gate B is held by sign_topology_clean (the still-loaded audits predate the supplemental edges) and Gate D remains pending, so SOLVED is forbidden.
decision.if_v1_closes: If and only if every gate closes, v1 would establish the following, and nothing wider. Within the frozen Li--Li--Liao unequal-mass non-hierarchical catalog on the declared domain m1 in [0.8,1.1], m2 in [0.7,1.2] at m3 = 1, and under one declared normalization and continuation gauge, the catalog behaves as a single continuation-connected sheet rather than the two families a scale-invariant projection appears to show; and on that sheet the planar linear-Floquet stability boundary can be decomposed into mechanism-specific arcs (+1 crossings, -1 crossings, and trace collisions) that meet at a small number of mixed (4,4) organizers, with representative events reproduced by an independent arbitrary-precision implementation and physical symplectic-quotient diagnostics rather than by deletion of trivial multipliers. That is a finite, numerical, resolution-bounded statement about one published catalog under one gauge. It is not a theorem, not a statement about the general three-body problem, not a statement about nonlinear or KAM stability, not a statement about spatial (non-planar) stability, and not a claim of priority.

gates.title: Independent truth for every mechanism word used in the paper
gates.criterion: A +1, -1, mixed, or Hamiltonian-Hopf/Krein label may appear as an ATLAS result only after independent BigFloat correction, event localization, and physical symplectic-quotient diagnostics at the exact bracket. The paper currently uses only the bound +1, Hamiltonian-Hopf, and three mixed organizers.

gates.title: Complete mechanism-resolved Floquet critical graph on the connected family sheet
gates.criterion: Every catalog S/U cell belongs to exactly one mechanism-specific polyline; N edges need not equal 620; every endpoint is a domain boundary, mixed organizer, or verified fold; mixed germs come from continuation artifacts; Newton-failed is forbidden; completeness is frozen; V1_CRITICAL_GRAPH.json has release_ready true.

gates.title: One continuation-connected family
gates.criterion: Family identity is bidirectional continuation in the Li chart and a generic strict-periodic chart, after rank and worst-MST attacks. Projected (T,L) branches are not families.

gates.title: Solved-release freeze
gates.criterion: Assembler release_ready, same-day novelty, manuscript generated only from release_claim records, --require-solved on the tagged commit.

claims.statement: Within the frozen Li--Li--Liao catalog and the declared v1 gauge, the evidence supports a single continuation-connected component: the 135,445-row mass-grid adjacency graph is connected (270,087 adjacency edges), and every one of the 26 adversarially selected links that could have separated it was crossed bidirectionally by continuation in the Li chart. Chart-independence was tested on one of those 26 -- the pathological invariant-near-duplicate bridge -- which was repeated in a generic translation-reduced strict-periodic chart outside the Li ansatz; the other 25 were not repeated in a second chart. Explicit absence of branch hysteresis is recorded for the 5 macroscopic bottlenecks. No surviving rank-loss, directionality, chart-dependence, or worst-MST obstruction to connectivity was found. The competing two-set reading is a reading of the scale-invariant (T,L) projection, which on this sheet is demonstrably folded and non-injective, so two visible branches there do not by themselves establish two dynamical families.
claims.method: Full-catalog adjacency plus bidirectional Li-chart continuation of 5 macroscopic MST cuts, 1 pathological invariant-near-duplicate bridge (which was additionally crossed in a generic strict-periodic chart, so it counts once as a link and twice as a chart), and the 20 globally worst MST chart jumps (run 31877974928) with no surviving disconnection; plus a 647-point shooting-rank recensus with tight re-correction of the 28 lowest-rank samples.
limitations: Numerical continuation statement for the declared catalog domain, not a theorem about the full planar three-body moduli space.

Continuation was certified on 26 distinct adversarially chosen links (5 macroscopic bottlenecks, 1 invariant-near-duplicate bridge, the 20 globally worst MST chart jumps), not on all 135,444 MST edges; connectivity across the remainder rests on 0.001-grid adjacency plus the absence of any surviving obstruction. The bridge is one link crossed in two charts and must not be counted as two links.

Chart-independence is demonstrated on exactly one of the 26 links. Per research/V1_CONNECTIVITY_CERTIFICATE_2026-08-15.md item 4, only the pathological invariant-near-duplicate bridge was repeated in a generic strict-periodic chart; the 5 macroscopic bottlenecks and the 20 worst MST edges are Li-chart results. 'Without branch hysteresis' is recorded only for the 5 bottlenecks (certificate item 2); it is not asserted for the other 21 links.
A negative adversarial search cannot exclude a separation finer than the 0.001 catalog grid, or outside the declared domain m1 in [0.8,1.1], m2 in [0.7,1.2] at m3=1.

'One component' is the decomposition best supported by this evidence under this gauge. It is not a disproof of the 2023 analysis on its own (T,L) terms, and it is not a statement about families of the general three-body problem.

claims.statement: On the slice m1=0.8023446113666945 with m3=1, the lower stability change of the sheet is bracketed at m2 in [0.7540187211922449, 0.7540187227698909] (width 1.58e-9) by a sign change of the event function, and is independently reproduced in a separate Julia BigFloat stack, with canonical Jacobi monodromy and physical E^omega/E diagnostics, as a physical +1 crossing of the reduced return map. Across that bracket the smaller-m2 flank carries a real reciprocal pair off the unit circle and the larger-m2 flank is elliptic.
claims.method: Independent Julia BigFloat Vern9 correction and event bisection to a sign-change bracket, then canonical Jacobi monodromy and physical E^omega/E evaluation on both flanks (run 31886247498).
limitations: Planar linear Floquet only. One bracketed representative on one m1 slice; it does not certify the mechanism along the rest of the +1 edge.
Flank spectra are evaluated at a fixed +/-5e-6 offset in m2, not as a limit at the critical point.
A sign-change bracket at 60 digits localizes a root of the computed event function; it is not an interval-arithmetic existence proof and does not separately certify transversality.

claims.statement: On the slice m1=0.8022889780964406 with m3=1, the upper stability change of the sheet is bracketed at m2 in [0.7592347034247101, 0.7592347096924873] (width 6.27e-9) by a sign change of the event function, and is independently reproduced in a separate Julia BigFloat stack as an opposite-Krein Hamiltonian-Hopf collision. The stable flank has two upper-half unit modes of opposite Krein sign; the unstable flank opens a reciprocal complex quartet (radius deviation 1.83e-2).
claims.method: Independent Julia BigFloat event bracket plus physical E^omega/E Krein diagnostics on both flanks of that bracket (run 31886247498).
limitations: Hamiltonian-Hopf wording is authorized only at this exact bracket, not at neighboring catalog rows.
Flank spectra are evaluated at a fixed +/-5e-6 offset in m2, not as a limit at the critical point.
A sign-change bracket at 60 digits localizes a root of the computed event function; it is not an interval-arithmetic existence proof and does not separately certify the collision's nondegeneracy.

claims.statement: Near each of the three coarse +1/-1 mechanism switches visible on the published 0.001 grid there is a root of the simultaneous conditions G+=G-=0, that is, a preimage of the universal spectral vertex (alpha,beta)=(4,4): principal-left (0.9292391921, 0.8853664625), secondary-left (0.9967681995, 0.9560193602), principal-right (1.0495531867, 1.1294758073). Each root was found by float64 mass-eliminated Newton and then recomputed at 60 digits by an independent Julia BigFloat mass Newton with canonical Jacobi monodromy and physical E^omega/E classification.
claims.method: Float64 mass-eliminated Newton for G+=G-=0, then independent Julia BigFloat mass Newton and physical E^omega/E classification (run 31886247456).
limitations: 0-D roots, not yet event-arc germs. A possible fourth mixed organizer at the secondary-right death is not claimed.

The three frozen artifacts declare themselves at the 'high_precision_supported' rung of the evidence ladder, not at 'independently_reproduced'; only the two headline events reach the higher rung. This claim must not be worded as an independent reproduction.
Each root is localized by Newton residual (relative event norm of order 1e-14), not by a sign-change bracket or interval arithmetic.

Identifying a coarse grid switch with the nearby root is a proximity argument at the 0.001 grid resolution. The assembler binds continuation germs within GERM_ATTACH_DISTANCE = 0.008 in mass; measured on the release configuration that threshold reproduces the committed twelve-attachment assembly only on the half-open window [0.006837, 0.008317), 1.216x wide (largest accepted attachment 0.006837449, nearest rejected mode-matching candidate 0.008316625). Re-derive with scripts/audit_germ_attachment_window.py.

GERM_ATTACH_DISTANCE does double duty: it caps how far a germ may sit from its organizer AND how far an edge endpoint may sit from that germ. Those compose, so the effective organizer-to-endpoint reach is up to 0.016 -- twice the number the constant appears to state, and 16 grid steps.

The germ step is not uniform across the three organizers. mixed_secondary_left was traced at --step 0.003 rather than the 7.5e-4 default (.github/workflows/headline-mixed-germs.yml), chosen specifically so its minus_one germ would travel far enough to bring cell 392's endpoint -- 8.59e-3 from the organizer -- inside the attachment radius. The check that keeps this honest: it did not also reach the secondary_left_birth blocker, whose endpoint (minus_one_s_to_u_0 start) remains 2.81e-2 from the organizer and 2.6379e-2 from the nearest germ, past even the composed 0.016 reach.

claims.statement: On the frozen 0.001 grid, each of the 620 published adjacent S/U cells contains an endpoint-sign-changing smooth event, and exactly one such event was localized per cell: 198 +1, 168 -1, and 254 trace collisions, falling on four macroscopic tracks with three coarse junctions.
claims.method: Full-catalog endpoint Floquet census, float64 prefilter with independent Julia BigFloat escalation on the 158 cells the prefilter missed.
limitations: Screening topology only. Not the exact connected critical graph.
An endpoint sign change cannot detect an even number of events inside one cell, so 'one event per cell' is a resolution-limited statement about the 0.001 grid, not a count of the critical set.
The maximum |event| over the 620 localized roots is 1.9898e-8 against the frozen gate of 2e-8, so the census clears the gate by about 0.5 percent; 165 of the 620 roots sit above 1e-8.

claims.statement: The secondary lobe birth is consistent with a G- m1-projection fold near (0.9957, 0.9743), distinct from the later secondary mixed organizer.
limitations: Not a release fold. Event-specific geometry and BigFloat nondegeneracy remain.
Float64 screening only, and a root-count change is consistent with a fold but does not identify one. The word 'fold' is not authorized for the paper.
A prior geometry screen for this endpoint was invalidated on audit for selecting the extreme minus-one roots at m1=0.996 and skipping the intervening S->U wall.

claims.statement: The physical soft +1 direction admits a generic same-period daughter that continues at least 18 float64 steps away from the Li parent (parent distance up to about 0.029) with no reconnect in that window.
claims.method: Generic pseudo-arclength in the strict-periodic chart.
limitations: Independent BigFloat of the minus representative is required before a branch class.
Float64 continuation over a finite window. 'No reconnect in that window' is not 'no reconnect'; no_branch_attachment and falsified remain admissible closes.
The word 'daughter' describes a candidate branch, not a verified bifurcation.

known_limitations: This is not a solution of the general three-body problem. Every result here is scoped to one published catalog, one declared gauge, and planar linear Floquet stability.
The mechanism-resolved critical graph is not finished. SOLVED is forbidden.
v1 'stable' means planar linear Floquet stability only: not nonlinear stability, not KAM stability, not spatial (non-planar) stability.
Gate A pass is scoped to mechanism words the paper is allowed to use. Fold, fourth mixed, and daughter labels remain unauthorized.
The one-family statement is a numerical continuation certificate for the declared catalog domain.
Negative literature searches are not a novelty theorem, and no priority claim ('first', 'the first') is authorized.

'Completeness' is bounded, and its bound is small. The frozen stability-neck raster (research/evidence/V1_NECK_RASTER_2026-08-16.json) covers m1 in [0.997,0.999] x m2 in [0.993,1.012] at step 1e-4 -- 4011 corrected samples, all 21 lines 'separated', interior_merge 0, truncation_undecidable 0, minimum resolved unstable gap 3.0e-4, maximum shooting residual 4.7807e-10. That rectangle is 0.0253% of the declared domain m1 in [0.8,1.1] x m2 in [0.7,1.2]. Derive the figure with scripts/completeness_scope.py, which reads the rectangle from the MERGE job of .github/workflows/stability-neck-scan.yml, cross-checks it against the committed raster artifact, and takes the domain from DECLARED_DOMAIN in scripts/assemble_critical_graph.py.

The other completeness input is not a sample of the domain outside that rectangle. All 12 proposals in research/evidence/V1_AL_POCKET_SCREEN_2026-08-15.json lie in ONE pocket at the principal lower transition, m1 in [0.80005, 0.80276] x m2 in [0.75266, 0.75407] -- an area fraction of 2.539e-5, i.e. 0.002539% of the declared domain -- and that artifact declares itself 'AI proposals plus float64 screening only; not scientific discovery evidence'. Outside the neck rectangle and that pocket, completeness rests on the published 0.001 grid alone. Both facts must travel with the screen wherever it is cited as completeness support, because it is one of the two inputs to the frozen certificate; they are now carried by the certificate's own scope description too (research/evidence/V1_COMPLETENESS_CERTIFICATE_2026-08-16.json, active_learning.extent and note), which src/threebody_atlas/completeness.py emits for every future freeze.

The 620/620 critical-root census clears the frozen event gate with little room: maximum |event| is 1.9898e-8 against the frozen gate of 2e-8, a margin of about 0.5 percent, and 165 of the 620 roots exceed 1e-8. Verify from research/evidence/V1_HYBRID_CRITICAL_ROOTS_2026-08-15.json.

A float64 re-evaluation of a published organizer chart is not reproducible and must never be used as a gate check. Re-evaluating the three canonical 60-digit organizer charts with the repository's float64 stack gives plus_one events that vary strongly with the machine: principal-left about -1.28e-7 to -1.35e-7, secondary-left about -1.96e-8 to -2.30e-8, and principal-right about -2.56e-8 to -8.66e-8, the last a factor of 3.4 spread measured across macOS arm64 and two different x86_64 Linux machines. Secondary-left's range straddles the frozen 2e-8 gate, so that organizer clears it on one machine and misses it on another. A quantity moving that much under a change of libm, BLAS or CPU is dominated by accumulated float64 integration error rather than by the dynamics. This is a limitation of float64 evaluation, not of the organizers: at 60 digits the same charts give relative plus_one events of order 1e-14. Any float64 reproduction of an organizer must therefore be re-corrected, never merely re-evaluated.

The assembled graph is not yet one connected object, and it is not the complete critical set. Taking research/evidence/V1_CRITICAL_GRAPH.json as committed, the edge incidence yields three components among the edge-incident nodes ({domain_m1_min_m2_0p761, domain_m2_max_m1_1p053}, {interior_terminus_plus_one_sweep_component_12_start, interior_terminus_plus_one_sweep_component_12_end}, and the merged catalog-plus-event-sign sheet through mixed_principal_left / mixed_secondary_left / mixed_principal_right); three further declared nodes (both headline event representatives and the daughter) have no edge incidence at all. There are now no unexplained nodes and no unclassified edge ends. The 620 catalog cells still sit on seven S/U polylines; six further event-sign polylines (133 certified roots, frozen 2e-8 / 1e-7) were ingested from the full-domain sweep so that interior 2→1 / 1→2 curves are no longer structurally invisible. Two isolated single-lattice detections (sweep components 5 and 11) remain certified vertices rather than edges. The still-loaded 2026-08-16 sign-topology audits were taken against the seven-edge catalog graph and still report missing curves, so release_ready is held false by the sign_topology_clean conjunct until those audits are re-run against the thirteen-edge graph. Continuation-connectedness of the family sheet (Gate C) is a different statement from connectedness of this critical graph, and does not imply it.

Germ attachment is threshold-dependent, and the threshold does double duty. The assembler binds an edge end to a mixed organizer when the mass distance is at most GERM_ATTACH_DISTANCE = 0.008, and the same constant caps how far a germ may sit from its own organizer, so the effective organizer-to-endpoint reach is up to 0.016. Auditing the release configuration shows the committed twelve-attachment assembly keeps every attachment it has only for thresholds on the half-open window [0.006837, 0.008317), 1.216x wide: the largest accepted attachment is 0.006837449 and the nearest rejected mode-matching candidate is 0.008316625 (plus_one_sweep_component_12 end <-> mixed_principal_right). The assembled graph does not visibly change until 0.008316625 (1.216x), where that leftover plus_one stub would glue to mixed_principal_right. Re-derive with scripts/audit_germ_attachment_window.py.

One germ trace was tuned to reach an endpoint. The mixed_secondary_left germs were traced at --step 0.003 instead of the 7.5e-4 default, chosen so the minus_one germ would travel far enough to bring cell 392's endpoint (8.59e-3 from the organizer) inside the attachment radius. The check that keeps that honest is that it did not also sweep up minus_one_s_to_u_0's start, which sits 2.81e-2 from the organizer and 2.6379e-2 from the nearest germ, beyond even the composed 0.016 reach. That endpoint is bound by the independently reproduced projection_fold classification, not by this threshold.

The novelty audit is stale against Gate D's own rule. Gate D demands a same-day literature search; the manifest records last_search_date 2026-08-15 with novelty.status 'pending'. See research/NOVELTY_AUDIT.md for what must be refreshed, and by whom, before any solved release.
Negative literature searches are not a novelty theorem.

The 620-cell census passes the frozen 2e-8 event gate by 0.511%, not comfortably. Maximum |event| is 1.9897980818583960e-08 = 99.489% of the gate (research/evidence/V1_HYBRID_CRITICAL_ROOTS_2026-08-15.json); 165 of 620 roots exceed 1e-8 and 7 exceed 95% of the gate. No sentence may report that the census 'passes the 2e-8 gate' without reporting that margin.

That margin is smaller than the uncertainty of the quantity it constrains. Re-evaluating the event functional at the exact recorded state, with the locked numpy 2.5.2 / scipy 1.18.0, across integrator tolerances rtol 5e-13 to 5e-14 moves it by a median 1.48e-7 -- 7.4x the gate -- and 20 of 24 probed cells (worst offenders and evenly spaced controls alike) cross 2e-8 at some tight tolerance (research/evidence/V1_EVENT_MARGIN_AUDIT_2026-08-16.json). The float64 lane's accepted residuals sit below its own evaluation noise floor for the ~165 cells in the top decade, so |event| <= 2e-8 certifies the localizer's stopping rule, not the distance to the true root.

The float64 residuals are not reproducible across CPU architectures at gate scale. 'reevaluated_at_accepting_tolerance' is bit-for-bit the computation that produced each recorded float64 residual, on the recorded state, and reproduces every digit when re-run on one machine; against the frozen CI values it differs by a median 2.78e-8 (1.39x the gate) and a maximum 4.14e-7 (20.7x the gate), and 10 of 22 comparable probes land above 2e-8. The cause is the ~8-digit cancellation in the event functionals (Delta = (alpha-4)^2 - 4(beta - 4 alpha + 8) with alpha, beta of order 1) sitting on top of architecture-dependent BLAS summation inside the monodromy product.

The independent Julia BigFloat lane does not escape this: its localizer also terminates on the first iterate below 2e-8, so 7 of its 158 roots are recorded at 1e-8 to 1.66e-8 despite dps=40 arithmetic capable of 1e-30. Those seven are gate-limited, not precision-limited.

The worst cells scatter rather than cluster, which is the signature of a measurement floor and not of physics: among the 25 worst, event-mode enrichment is 1.27/1.00/0.59, orientation enrichment 1.07/0.93, twelve distinct m1 bands, Spearman correlation of |event| with m1 of 0.12, and median organizer distance 0.054 against a census median of 0.049. The floor is quantified: the monodromy invariants alpha and beta are themselves reproducible only to a median relative 4.2e-9 across the tolerance ladder, and the event functionals cancel by a median factor 2.6e8 (worst 5.2e10).

Pulling max |event| down 10x to 2e-9 is impossible in the float64 lane at any integrator tolerance -- the target is 73x below that lane's own evaluation uncertainty -- and requires routing all 620 cells through the BigFloat lane at dps=40 with a 2e-9 stopping tolerance. Measured cost: mean 5.45 secant iterations per cell over 204 recorded BigFloat cells, ~23 min per cell at the CI-measured correction cost, ~179 serial CPU-hours, under 3 wall-hours at the existing 62-way fan-out.

The census root locations are far more robust than the census certificate. With the measured d(event)/d(m2) of 20 to 660 per unit mass, even the full evaluation uncertainty maps to an m2 uncertainty of 1e-10 to 8e-9, well inside the 1e-3 published cells. The topology of the graph is not in question; the numerical certificate attached to it is.
